name: Rocket.Chat
description: Rocket.Chat is an open-source communications platform for team chat, channels, direct messages, file sharing, voice and video calls, and omnichannel customer support. This script performs a manual (non-Docker) install of the official prebuilt Meteor server bundle, backed by a local MongoDB.

app_vars.name: var_admin_email
app_vars.label: Admin Email
app_vars.help: Email address for the generated admin account. Rocket.Chat needs a valid address here; it is not used to send mail unless you configure SMTP.

notes.text: Log in at http://IP:3000 as `admin`; the generated password is in `~/rocketchat.creds` inside the container. The setup wizard is skipped deliberately: its final step mails a confirmation code, and a fresh install has no mail server configured, so the wizard cannot be completed and would lock you out of the admin account it just created.
The admin password is generated, not chosen. Change it, and review the admin email, before real use. If you kept the default admin@example.com, set a real address in Admin > Users.

The install downloads the official prebuilt server bundle (~250 MB) and compiles native npm modules, so it takes several minutes. The service needs roughly 20-30 seconds after start before the web UI answers.

ROOT_URL in /etc/rocketchat/rocketchat.env is set to the container IP. Change it to the public URL and restart with `systemctl restart rocketchat` before putting Rocket.Chat behind a reverse proxy or domain, otherwise logins, uploads and OAuth redirects break.

MongoDB runs as a single-node replica set (rs0), which Rocket.Chat 8.x requires: it dropped oplog tailing in 8.0 and relies on change streams and multi-document transactions. Do not convert mongod back to standalone.
All chat data lives in the local MongoDB (database `rocketchat`, files in /var/lib/mongodb). Back that up together with /etc/rocketchat/rocketchat.env.
